o2_persona_dia: An astronaut breathes about 0.82 kg of oxygen per day.
agua_persona_dia: At a planetary base, NASA estimates about 3.4 kg of water per astronaut per day: 2 for drinking, 0.5 to prepare food, 0.4 for hygiene and 0.5 for the toilet.
comida_persona_dia: Each astronaut eats about 1.5 kg of food per day (1.51 kg without packaging, according to NASA).
recuperacion_agua: The International Space Station recovers 98 % of the water the crew uses.
agua_por_kg_o2: To make 1 kg of oxygen by splitting water (2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂), 1.125 kg of water is used.
fsp_kw: NASA's Fission Surface Power reactor is designed to deliver 40 kW continuously, day and night.
fsp_masa_t: NASA asked for the surface reactor to weigh less than 6 tonnes.
ciclo_lunar_dias: A full day on the Moon (sunrise to sunrise) lasts about 29.5 Earth days: almost 15 days of light and almost 15 of night.
dosis_luna_msv_dia: On the surface of the Moon, without protection, you receive about 1.37 mSv of radiation per day: about 2.6 times more than inside the International Space Station.
dosis_marte_msv_dia: Curiosity's RAD instrument measured about 0.64 mSv per day on the surface of Mars.
limite_carrera_msv: NASA limits the radiation an astronaut can receive over their whole career to 600 mSv.
tormenta_mayo_2024: Between May 9 and 13, 2024, NASA recorded 14 solar particle events and a Kp 9 geomagnetic storm, the strongest in 20 years. On the Moon there is no atmosphere or magnetic field for protection: the crew must go to the shelter.
gravedad_luna: The Moon's gravity is 1.62 m/s², one sixth of Earth's.
veggie: On the ISS, the Veggie system has already grown lettuce, radishes and peppers that astronauts ate.
lcross_hielo: In 2009 NASA's LCROSS mission impacted Cabeus crater, at the lunar south pole, and measured that its soil contains about 5.6 % water ice.
moxie_o2: MOXIE, aboard the Perseverance rover, made oxygen from Martian CO₂: up to 12 g per hour and 122 g in total. A plant for astronauts would need to be hundreds of times larger.
polvo_marte_2018: In 2018 a dust storm covered all of Mars for weeks and blocked the Sun so much that the Opportunity rover, which ran on solar panels, lost power forever.
luz_marte: Mars is 1.5 times farther from the Sun than Earth, so it gets less than half the sunlight: panels produce much less.
tormenta_marte_mayo_2024: In May 2024 a solar storm reached Mars. The Curiosity rover's RAD instrument measured the biggest radiation surge since it landed in 2012: for an astronaut standing next to it, it would have been like about 30 chest X-rays.
retraso_tierra_marte: A radio signal takes about 4 minutes between Earth and Mars when they are closest, and about 24 minutes when they are farthest apart.
